note.en: An order management platform where every question was answered and every answer had a source. The register is short on purpose: this is what a pass looks like when the room actually knows its platform.
note.de: Eine Auftragsplattform, bei der jede Frage beantwortet war und jede Antwort einen Beleg hatte. Das Register ist absichtlich kurz: so sieht ein Durchgang aus, wenn der Raum seine Plattform wirklich kennt.

head.decision_question: Should RetailCore OMS be migrated to a cloud-native event-driven architecture by Q2 2027?
head.decision_owner: VP Engineering (named in intake, redacted for the public fixture)
head.in_scope: Order intake, order state machine, fulfilment dispatch, event distribution to the three consuming teams
head.out_of_scope: Payment provider integration, warehouse robotics control, the retail web frontend
head.deadline: Decision by 2026-11-30; scoped delivery window Q2 2027

Q1.1.text: Order processing latency has increased from avg 120ms to 950ms over 6 months.
Q1.1.source: Monitoring dashboard, exported 2026-08-01, owned by Ops team.

Q1.2.text: The situation has developed over roughly 6 months. The review was triggered when the fulfilment team's SLA breach count crossed 12 in July 2026.
Q1.2.source: SLA breach log, Fulfilment Ops, July 2026 extract.

Q1.3.text: Named by the Head of Fulfillment. The platform team agrees on the symptom; Analytics considers latency secondary to their batch export gaps.

Q1.4.text: Two attempts: connection-pool tuning (Feb 2026, partial relief for 3 weeks) and a read-replica for the analytics export (May 2026, held).

Q1.5.text: Cost of inaction is quantified at 240,000 EUR over 12 months in SLA credits and manual reprocessing effort.

Q2.1.text: Should RetailCore OMS be migrated to a cloud-native event-driven architecture by Q2 2027?

Q2.2.text: VP Engineering is the accountable decision owner; named in the intake, redacted here.

Q2.3.text: Order intake, order state machine, fulfilment dispatch, event distribution to the three consuming teams.

Q2.4.text: Payment provider integration, warehouse robotics control, the retail web frontend.

Q2.5.text: Decision deadline 2026-11-30. If it passes, the current capex allocation returns to the general pool and the review restarts in the FY2027 cycle.

Q2.6.text: p95 order processing latency below 300ms, zero SLA breaches per quarter, and analytics export completing within its 04:00 window.
Q2.6.source: Decision charter DC-2026-07, success criteria section.

Q2.7.text: Head of Fulfillment (SLA breaches), Head of Analytics (export window), VP Engineering (operational cost per order).

Q3.1.text: PostgreSQL remains the system of record; the company's approved cloud provider is fixed by an existing enterprise agreement.

Q3.2.text: Budget envelope: up to 800,000 EUR capex + 120,000 EUR annual opex uplift.

Q3.3.text: 8 years in production. Change cadence: roughly 2 releases per month, with a quarterly freeze around peak trading.

Q3.4.text: Annual PCI-adjacent scope review each January constrains any change touching order records; no other audit commitment applies.

Q3.5.text: Architecture board review, then CFO capex sign-off. Historically 6 to 8 weeks end to end.
Q3.5.source: Governance handbook v4, plus last three decisions ARC-2025-12, ARC-2025-19, ARC-2026-03.

Q4.1.text: Java monolith (8 years, Java 17 after a 2023 uplift), PostgreSQL 14, a batch export job, and an internal admin UI.

Q4.2.text: Confluence architecture space; last verified against the running system during the June 2026 inventory.

Q4.3.text: No dark zone remains: the last unowned component (a legacy pricing hook) was documented and covered by tests in the June 2026 inventory.

Q4.4.text: Order, customer reference, and fulfilment state. PostgreSQL is the single source; customer master lives in CRM and is referenced, not copied.

Q4.5.text: Three documented integrations (fulfilment, customer service, analytics) plus a documented CRM read. No undocumented integrations found in the June inventory.

Q4.6.text: Automated coverage 74% line, 81% on the order state machine. Last full regression run 2026-08-05.

Q5.1.text: Fulfilment (sync REST), customer service (sync REST), analytics (nightly batch export).

Q5.2.text: Fulfilment is business-critical: 99.5% availability, p95 under 400ms. Customer service is important but tolerates degradation. Analytics is batch, no latency requirement.

Q5.3.text: No shadow copies found. The June inventory reconciled 90 days of API access logs against the integration register with no unaccounted caller.
Q5.3.source: API access log review, ARC-INV-2026-05 appendix B.

Q5.4.text: Fulfilment and customer service are covered by signed internal SLAs. The analytics export is contracted through a data-sharing agreement.

Q5.5.text: Named accept-authority per consumer is recorded in the SLA schedule; all three are current employees and reachable.

Q6.1.text: Order data is classified Internal; customer reference data is classified Confidential. Validated by the Data Protection Officer.

Q6.2.text: Personal data enters through the order intake API (name, delivery address, contact email). Legal basis: contract performance.
Q6.2.source: Record of processing activities ROPA-2026, entry 14.

Q6.3.text: Head of Commerce Operations owns order data; Head of CRM owns customer master.

Q6.4.text: Order records retained 7 years from last transaction per commercial law. The erasure path was tested end to end on 2026-04-22.
Q6.4.source: Retention policy RET-2025-01 and erasure test report ERT-2026-04.

Q6.5.text: All processing stays within the EU region of the approved cloud provider. No transfer outside the organisation's control.
Q6.5.source: Enterprise cloud agreement CLD-2024-01, data residency annex.

Q7.1.text: GDPR applies. PCI DSS applies to the payment path, which is out of scope for this decision. Reviewed by Compliance on 2026-01-15.

Q7.2.text: Last internal audit 2026-01. Two findings, both closed by 2026-03.
Q7.2.source: Internal audit report IA-2026-01 and closure record.

Q7.3.text: No AI/ML in the decision subject. AI is used only in the authoring process of this analysis.

Q7.4.text: Not applicable — AI/ML is not in the decision subject.

Q7.5.text: ISO 27001 certification is maintained at group level; the platform is in scope of the statement of applicability.

Q8.1.text: Three paths considered: in-place optimisation, event-driven rebuild with strangler cut-over, and a full rewrite. The full rewrite was set aside for delivery risk.

Q8.2.text: One irreversible step: the cut-over of the order state machine to the event store. Once orders are written there, the monolith's write path is decommissioned and cannot be restored without a data replay.

Q8.3.text: Dual-run of old and new order intake for one full quarter, including a peak-trading window, was considered and costed.

Q8.4.text: Rollback before the cut-over step is a configuration switch, under 1 hour, no data loss. After the cut-over, rollback requires a replay estimated at 12 hours with full fidelity retained.

Q8.5.text: Yes — evaluated and documented. Return after the cut-over is possible but costly; it is recorded as a dated decision point, not as a risk line.
Q8.5.source: Migration outline MIG-2026-02, decision point DP-3.

Q8.6.text: Historical orders under retention obligation migrate ahead of cut-over in a verified bulk load; the 7-year window is preserved.
Q8.6.source: Migration outline MIG-2026-02, data section, reviewed against RET-2025-01.

Q9.1.text: The Platform Engineering team owns RetailCore OMS; the accountable lead is named in the intake.
Q9.1.source: Org chart 2026-07 and service catalogue entry SVC-014.

Q9.2.text: Change requests arrive through the service catalogue, are triaged weekly, and are reviewed by two platform engineers. Handoffs stall most often at the analytics export contract.

Q9.3.text: Knowledge on the order state machine sits with three engineers; the June inventory removed the previous single-holder concentration.

Q9.4.text: No restructuring planned. One engineer joins the team in October 2026.

Q9.5.text: The Head of Fulfillment holds informal veto power: no previous OMS change has proceeded over their objection.

Q10.1.text: SLO: 99.5% monthly availability. Met: last 12 months 99.7%. Source: SRE runbook v3.
Q10.1.source: SRE runbook v3 and the 12-month availability report.

Q10.2.text: RTO 4 hours, RPO 15 minutes. Last restore test 2026-02-19, both targets met.

Q10.3.text: Structured logs, RED metrics on all endpoints, distributed traces on the order path. Alerts on SLO burn rate and on batch export overrun.

Q10.4.text: Documented incident process with a 24/7 on-call rota, and a change process with a peak-trading freeze. Both were exercised during the July SLA breaches.
Q10.4.source: SRE runbook v3 and incident records INC-2026-0712 ff.

Q10.5.text: Production access is role-based through the central identity provider and reviewed quarterly. Last review 2026-07-01.

Q10.6.text: Encrypted at rest (provider-managed volume encryption) and in transit (TLS 1.3). Keys are held in the central key vault, separate from the data.
